title: Psalms Chapter 135 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 135 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 135 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 135.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:1 instruct us to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:1 begins with the command to 'Praise ye the LORD.'

questions.question: Who are instructed to praise the name of the LORD according to Psalms 135:1?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically addresses 'O ye servants of the LORD' to praise Him.

questions.question: According to Psalms 135:3, why should we sing praises unto the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse states that we should sing praises unto His name because 'the LORD is good.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:4 say about Jacob and Israel?
options: They are chosen by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They are chosen by the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse declares that 'the LORD hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:5 declare about the LORD?
options: The LORD is a mighty warrior
questions.explanation: The verse begins with 'For I know that the LORD is great.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 135:6 states that the LORD does what pleases Him in heaven and earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:6 affirms that 'Whatsoever the LORD pleased, that did he in heaven, and in earth.'

questions.question: What natural phenomena does Psalms 135:7 mention that the LORD causes?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that 'He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 135:8 describes the LORD smiting only the firstborn of man in Egypt.
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:8 states that He smote 'the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast.'

questions.question: In Psalms 135:9, to whom did the LORD send tokens and wonders?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that the tokens and wonders were sent 'into the midst of thee, O Egypt.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 135:10 mentions that the LORD smote great nations.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that 'Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:15 say about the idols of the heathen?
options: They are made of silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: They are made of silver and gold
questions.explanation: The verse describes idols as 'silver and gold, the work of men's hands.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 135:19, which group is called to bless the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically calls out 'Bless the LORD, O house of Israel.'

questions.question: Who dwells in Zion according to Psalms 135:21?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, which dwelleth at Jerusalem.'

questions.question: In what order does Psalms 135 instruct the servants of the LORD to act?
questions.explanation: The chapter opens with a command to 'Praise ye the LORD,' followed by instructions to sing praises, and bless the LORD.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 135 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 135 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD is the one who smote the firstborn of Egypt, as mentioned in Psalms 135:8.

questions.question: What did the LORD send into the midst of Egypt upon Pharaoh and his servants?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:9 specifies that the LORD sent tokens and wonders into Egypt upon Pharaoh and his servants.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is described as being above all gods in Psalms 135.
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:5 states that the LORD is great and above all gods, affirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: Which kings did the LORD smite according to Psalms 135?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:10-11 mentions Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, who were defeated by the LORD.

questions.question: What heritage did the LORD give unto Israel?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 135:12, the LORD gave the land of Canaan as an heritage unto Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The idols of the heathen are described as having the ability to speak and see.
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:16-17 indicates that the idols have mouths and eyes but cannot speak or see, making the statement false.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:14 say about the LORD's relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will judge His people, indicating His active role in their lives as mentioned in Psalms 135:14.

questions.question: How does Psalms 135:13 emphasize the enduring nature of the LORD's name?
options: It is only for a season
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:13 asserts that the name of the LORD endureth forever, highlighting its eternal significance.

questions.question: True or False: Those who make idols are compared to the idols themselves in Psalms 135.
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:18 states that those who make idols are like them, affirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: According to Psalms 135, how should the house of Levi respond to the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:20 instructs the house of Levi to bless the LORD, reflecting a proper response to God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:3 say about the nature of the LORD's goodness?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD is good and that singing praises to His name is pleasant, as noted in Psalms 135:3.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned about trust in God from Psalms 135:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:6 illustrates that whatsoever the LORD pleased, He did in heaven and earth, encouraging trust in His sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:4 indicate about Israel's relationship with the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:4 states that the LORD has chosen Jacob (Israel) as His peculiar treasure, indicating a special relationship.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 135 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 135.

questions.question: What are the idols of the heathen made of, according to Psalms 135?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the work of men's hands' (Psalms 135:15), indicating their material composition.

questions.question: According to Psalms 135:16, what do the idols lack?
questions.explanation: 'They have ears, but they hear not; neither is there any breath in their mouths' (Psalms 135:17) emphasizes that idols are lifeless.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:18 say about those who make idols?
options: They that make them are like unto them
questions.correctAnswer: They that make them are like unto them
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'They that make them are like unto them: so is every one that trusteth in them' (Psalms 135:18), indicating a spiritual deadness.

questions.question: Who is called to bless the LORD in Psalms 135:19?
questions.explanation: 'Bless the LORD, O house of Israel: bless the LORD, O house of Aaron' (Psalms 135:19) specifically mentions these groups.

questions.question: In Psalms 135:20, who besides the house of Levi is instructed to bless the LORD?
questions.explanation: 'Ye that fear the LORD, bless the LORD' (Psalms 135:20) indicates that all who revere God are called to bless Him.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned in Psalms 135:21 as the dwelling place of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 'Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, which dwelleth at Jerusalem' (Psalms 135:21) highlights Zion as the location of God's presence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 135:14 states that the LORD will judge His people.
questions.explanation: The verse declares, 'For the LORD will judge his people' (Psalms 135:14), affirming that God holds His people accountable.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:5 say about the LORD in comparison to other gods?
questions.explanation: 'For I know that the LORD is great, and that our Lord is above all gods' (Psalms 135:5) asserts God's supremacy over other deities.

questions.question: According to Psalms 135:7, what does the LORD bring out of His treasuries?
questions.explanation: 'He causeth the vapours to ascend... he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries' (Psalms 135:7) indicates God's control over natural elements.

questions.question: Which historical event does Psalms 135:8 refer to regarding Egypt?
questions.explanation: 'Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast' (Psalms 135:8) refers to the tenth plague during the Exodus.

questions.question: True or False: The name of the LORD endures for a limited time according to Psalms 135:13.
questions.explanation: 'Thy name, O LORD, endureth for ever' (Psalms 135:13) clearly states that God's name is everlasting.

questions.question: Which king is mentioned in Psalms 135:10 as having been smote?
questions.explanation: 'Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings; Sihon king of the Amorites' (Psalms 135:10-11) identifies Sihon as a defeated king.

questions.question: Which literary device is prevalent in Psalms 135 regarding the idols?
questions.explanation: The verses about idols utilize parallelism, where similar ideas are expressed in successive lines, enhancing the message (Psalms 135:16-17).

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament echoes the theme of the futility of idols similar to Psalms 135?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 8:4 states that 'an idol is nothing in the world', paralleling the futility of idols highlighted in Psalms 135.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 135 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 135 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:3 teach about the nature of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:3 states, 'Praise the LORD; for the LORD is good: sing praises unto his name; for it is pleasant.' This emphasizes God's intrinsic goodness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 135:4, whom has the LORD chosen for himself?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:4 declares, 'For the LORD hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure,' indicating God's choice of Jacob.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:6 reveal about God's sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:6 states, 'Whatsoever the LORD pleased, that did he in heaven, and in earth,' showing His absolute sovereignty over all creation.

questions.question: Who did the LORD smite according to Psalms 135:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:8 mentions, 'Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast,' demonstrating God's judgment on Egypt.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:15 say about the idols of the heathen?
options: They are the work of men's hands
questions.correctAnswer: They are the work of men's hands
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:15 states, 'The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the work of men's hands,' highlighting their created and powerless nature.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:13 say about the name of the LORD?
options: It is known only to a few
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:13 asserts, 'Thy name, O LORD, endureth for ever,' indicating the eternal nature of God's name.

questions.question: In Psalms 135:10, which kings does it mention that the LORD smote?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:10 references, 'Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings; Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan,' showing God's power over nations.

questions.question: What is indicated by the phrase 'Ye that stand in the house of the LORD' in Psalms 135:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:2 addresses 'Ye that stand in the house of the LORD,' implying a call to the servants of God who worship in His presence.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is illustrated in Psalms 135:7 regarding His control over nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:7 illustrates God's sovereignty as it states, 'He causeth the vapours to ascend... he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.'

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 14 convey about God's nature?
options: God is great and judges His people
God does not act in history
questions.correctAnswer: God is great and judges His people
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 affirm God's greatness and sovereignty, while verse 14 states, 'For the LORD will judge his people,' combining His greatness with His role as judge.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:19-20 encourage the house of Levi to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:20 states, 'ye that fear the LORD, bless the LORD,' encouraging respect and reverence toward God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 135:18 imply about those who make idols?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:18 states, 'They that make them are like unto them,' implying that those who create and trust in idols become spiritually blind and powerless.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the work of men's hands' in Psalms 135:15 suggest about idols?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the work of men's hands' in Psalms 135:15 clearly indicates that idols are created by humans, lacking any divine nature.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that idols are as powerful as God. What does Psalms 135:15-17 actually teach?
options: Idols are made by humans and have no power
questions.correctAnswer: Idols are made by humans and have no power
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:15-17 illustrates that idols are 'the work of men's hands,' having mouths that do not speak, and eyes that do not see, highlighting their powerlessness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 135:21 conclude the chapter regarding God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalms 135:21 states, 'Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, which dwelleth at Jerusalem,' affirming God's presence in Jerusalem.
